newsitem.title: USA: IMM currency futures close mostly lower.
newsitem.headline: IMM currency futures close mostly lower.

text.p: IMM currency futures closed mostly lower, with September marks and Swiss francs ending near contract lows that were set during pit hours when the dollar powered higher.

After the close, San Francisco Federal Reserve president Robert Parry said the U.S. can't expect the dollar to appreciate "forever," and said the rising dollar was no permanent fix against inflation pressures.
The dollar has advanced 22 percent against the mark alone since the start of the year, and has pushed September marks and Swiss francs to consecutive contract lows.
September marks hit a contract low of $0.5324 after the dollar/mark rose to a 8-year high at 1.8830 spot. Meanwhile, September Swiss francs set a contract low of $0.6533.
Both contracts are expected to fall further in the near term, with marks eyeing $0.5302 or 1.8910 spot and Swiss franc futures crumbling to $0.6525 or 1.5394 spot.
Intraday selling in the mark and Swiss franc futures pits was contained as some dealers later took dollar/mark profits, currency analysts said.
Fears the Bundesbank may intervene against the dollar lingered in the market.

The Bundesbank denied on Tuesday that its central bank policy council was planning an emergency meeting on Wednesday, removing market speculation that the central bank would leave open the door for higher short-term German interest rates.
One currency analyst said he expects September marks to fall to $0.5278, or 1.90 spot by the end of the year. He holds a slim expectation that September could decline to $0.5143 or 1.95 spot marks.
"I don't see the U.S. hiking rates much more," he said.
Also, Germany's Ifo economic research institute said on Tuesday the Bundesbank might send a signal to currency markets if the dollar rose above 1.90 marks.
September yen remained near the bottom of the daily range at $0.008420. Fresh buy-stop orders at 119.30 spot kept September yen on the defensive at about $0.008431, he said.
September yen is expected to test support at $0.008392, or 119.80-85 spot.
Traders said September yen was expected to hold support at $0.008382, which equates to 120.00, an area expected to induce Bank of Japan (BOJ) dollar selling.

At the end of pit trade, September yen was down $0.000072 at $0.008430, marks fell $0.0035 to $0.5336, Swiss francs lost $0.0032 to $0.6552, sterling was down $0.0054 to $1.6208, Canadian dollars were off $0.0010 to $0.7261, Australian dollars were $0.0019 lower to $0.7402, and Mexican pesos climbed $0.000375 to $0.126250.
